{"metadata":{"description":"DeepSeek Harness plugin: raise Node's HTTP timeouts process-wide so slow local models (Ollama, LM Studio) are not cut off at 5 minutes","id":"gh:1351434803","install_available":true,"language":"JavaScript","name":"dsh-fetch-timeouts","slug":"d3vmeh/dsh-fetch-timeouts","topics":["deepseek-harness","dsh-plugin","ollama"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"DeepSeek Harness plugin: raise Node's HTTP timeouts process-wide so slow local models (Ollama, LM St"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"udio) are not cut off at 5 minutes"},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-fetch-timeouts"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"Raises Node's HTTP timeouts for the whole DeepSeek Harness process, so a slow local model is not cut"},{"id":"p3s2","text":" off after 5 minutes of silence."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"## The problem it fixes"},{"id":"p5s1","text":"Node's built-in `fetch` (which dsh's model adapters use) gives up when a server sends no response he"},{"id":"p5s2","text":"aders for 300 seconds, or no body bytes for 300 seconds. dsh has no setting for those two timers: `s"},{"id":"p5s3","text":"treamIdleTimeoutMs` is dsh's own watchdog and `timeoutMs` is the SDK's request timer, so raising the"},{"id":"p5s4","text":"m changes the failure message from `pi-ai stream idle timeout` to `Failure reason: terminated` (`UND"},{"id":"p5s5","text":"_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` / `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`) at exactly 5:00."},{"id":"p6s1","text":"Servers that stay silent that long include Ollama and LM Studio while a model thinks or generates a "},{"id":"p6s2","text":"large tool call (for example the entire contents of a file for `write`), and any backend that does n"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"ot send keepalive pings. llama.cpp's `llama-server` sends a ping every 30 seconds by default, so lla"},{"id":"p6s4","text":"ma.cpp users usually do not need this plugin."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"## Install"},{"id":"p8s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"That is enough: the defaults raise both timeouts to 30 minutes. To change them, add to `~/.dsh/profi"},{"id":"p9s2","text":"les/web/cordis.patch.yml`:"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"Restart `dsh web`. One line confirms it at startup:"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"Also raise dsh's own watchdog on the provider route, or it will fire first:"},{"id":"p14s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## What you should know"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"- It is process-wide. Every `fetch` that uses Node's global dispatcher (model calls, web search, HTT"},{"id":"p16s2","text":"P MCP servers, cloud providers) gets the same longer limits; `web_fetch` is not affected because it "},{"id":"p16s3","text":"builds its own per-request agent. A genuinely dead connection therefore takes up to the configured t"},{"id":"p16s4","text":"ime to be noticed, and once you have raised `streamIdleTimeoutMs` as well, dsh's idle watchdog is th"},{"id":"p16s5","text":"e only remaining backstop for a hung model server. Reasonable on a single-user machine; think twice "},{"id":"p16s6","text":"on a shared host.
- It works by wrapping Node's global fetch dispatcher so every request gets your t"},{"id":"p16s7","text":"imeouts. Whatever dispatcher was installed before keeps doing the routing, so the proxy that dsh 0.2"},{"id":"p16s8","text":" sets up from `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` keeps working. If `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` is s"},{"id":"p16s9","text":"et, the plugin uses undici's proxy-aware agent instead, as it did in 0.1.0. On dsh 0.2 you do not ne"},{"id":"p16s10","text":"ed that variable, and setting it swaps dsh's proxy rules for undici's, which differ slightly (for ex"},{"id":"p16s11","text":"ample on loopback addresses other than 127.0.0.1). Tested on Node 22 with undici 8 (undici 8 require"},{"id":"p16s12","text":"s Node 22.19 or newer). Confirmed by a user on Windows with Ollama on a 20 minute file write (discus"},{"id":"p16s13","text":"sion #4518).
- Loading the plugin's `undici` dependency already swaps Node's default dispatcher for "},{"id":"p16s14","text":"undici's own (same 300 second defaults); the plugin then applies your timeouts. undici only installs"},{"id":"p16s15","text":" its default when no global dispatcher exists yet, so another plugin loading undici later cannot rep"},{"id":"p16s16","text":"lace the plugin's wrapper. Unloading the plugin puts back the dispatcher it wrapped.
- It is a stopg"},{"id":"p16s17","text":"ap. When dsh exposes these timeouts itself (its pi-ai dependency already accepts a custom `fetch`), "},{"id":"p16s18","text":"this plugin becomes unnecessary."},{"id":"p17s1","text":"## License"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"MIT"}],"truncated":false}
